# TimeIndex::argsort

[Back to TimeIndex API Reference](../../timeindex_api_reference)

## Signature

```cpp
TimeIndex::argsort() const -> pluss::Series
```

## What It Does

Returns the integer permutation that would sort the index.

It is the reusable ordering plan. That is the distinction from `sort()`, which
returns the reordered axis directly.

## Returns

`pluss::Series`
    A 1D integer permutation.

## Examples

```cpp
auto dup = pluss::timeindex::make({
    "2024-11-01T00:40:00Z",
    "2024-11-01T00:00:00Z",
    "2024-11-01T00:20:00Z",
    "2024-11-01T00:20:00Z",
    "2024-11-01T01:00:00Z",
}, false);

auto out = dup.argsort();
std::cout << pluss::series::print(out) << "\n";
```

### Output

```text
Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 2, 3, 0, 4]
```

Example 2. Reuse the same permutation on the index and any aligned value
payload.

```cpp
auto order = dup.argsort();
auto sorted_idx = dup.take(order);
std::cout << pluss::series::print(order) << "\n";
std::cout << pluss::timeindex::print(sorted_idx) << "\n";
// values.take(order) would follow the same temporal order
```

## Notes

- `argsort()` is especially useful when you need to sort multiple aligned
  payloads the same way.

## See Also

- [`TimeIndex::sort`](sort.md)
- [`TimeIndex::take`](take.md)
